plan.topic_summary: 6G represents the next generational leap in wireless connectivity, and its intersection with space-based communications—non-terrestrial networks, direct-to-device service, constellation economics, and spectrum policy—is a defining question for the 1-5 year horizon as standards, launch costs, and regulatory frameworks converge.
key_questions: What spectrum bands are being allocated or proposed for 6G non-terrestrial use, and what regulatory decisions (ITU, FCC, national) are expected within the next 12 months?
How will constellation economics—launch cost per kilogram, satellite lifetime, required constellation size—evolve over 1-3 years to support 6G-grade service levels?
What are the realistic technical barriers and deployment timeline for direct-to-device 6G service, and which architectures (LEO, MEO, hybrid) are most likely to be viable within 3 years?
Will 6G standards (expected around 2030) be backward compatible with current non-terrestrial network architectures, or will a new ground segment and satellite generation be required?
What is the competitive and regulatory landscape between terrestrial 6G operators and space-based providers for the integrated space-ground network over a 3-5 year horizon?

sources.title: Operator's Perspective on 6G: 6G Services, Vision, and Spectrum
sources.abstract: 6G refers to the communication and services expected to emerge around 2030, coinciding with the convergence of service/terminal evolution and the evolution of mobile communication. Successful implementation of 6G necessitates collaborative efforts from all participants in emerging 6G ecosystems. This includes expanding the range of 6G usage scenarios, selecting appropriate candidate spectrum, and fostering open interfaces. Promising applications for 6G, such as artificial intelligence (AI), sensing, autonomous vehicles (AVs), urban air mobility (UAM), extended reality (XR), holograms, and digital twins, are under discussion. However, the identification of “killer services” unique to 6G and the development of innovative form factor devices are deemed crucial for delivering unprecedented customer experiences. This article reviews key lessons learned from the world's initial 5G commercialization, known as “5G Lessons Learned,” and subsequently presents perspectives on 6G usage scenarios and services anticipated to be implemented by 2030. Notably, simultaneous exploration of new spectrum and refarming of underutilized spec-trum in existing services are highlighted as imperative. As part of this initiative, we provide tangible measurement study results for high-frequency bands considered as potential 6G candidate spectrum.

sources.title: Emerging Advancements in 6G NTN Radio Access Technologies: An Overview
sources.abstract: The efforts on the development, standardization and improvements to communication systems towards 5G Advanced and 6G are on track to provide benefits such as an unprecedented level of connectivity and performance, enabling a diverse range of vertical services. The full integration of non-terrestrial components into 6G plays a pivotal role in realizing this paradigm shift towards ubiquitous communication and global coverage. However, this integration into 6G brings forth a set of its own challenges, particularly in Radio Access Technologies (RATs). To this end, this paper comprehensively discusses those challenges at different levels of RATs and proposes the corresponding potential emerging advancements in the realm of 6G NTN. In particular, the focus is on advancing the prospective aspects of Radio Resource Management (RRM), spectral coexistence in terrestrial and non-terrestrial components and flexible waveform design solutions to combat the impediments. This discussion with a specific focus on emerging advancements in 6G NTN RATs is critical for shaping the next generation networks and potentially relevant in contributing the part in standardization in forthcoming releases

sources.title: On the Road to 6G: Visions, Requirements, Key Technologies, and Testbeds
sources.abstract: Fifth generation (5G) mobile communication systems have entered the stage of commercial deployment, providing users with new services, improved user experiences as well as a host of novel opportunities to various industries. However, 5G still faces many challenges. To address these challenges, international industrial, academic, and standards organizations have commenced research on sixth generation (6G) wireless communication systems. A series of white papers and survey papers have been published, which aim to define 6G in terms of requirements, application scenarios, key technologies, etc. Although ITU-R has been working on the 6G vision and it is expected to reach a consensus on what 6G will be by mid-2023, the related global discussions are still wide open and the existing literature has identified numerous open issues. This paper first provides a comprehensive portrayal of the 6G vision, technical requirements, and application scenarios, covering the current common understanding of 6G. Then, a critical appraisal of the 6G network architecture and key technologies is presented. Furthermore, existing testbeds and advanced 6G verification platforms are detailed for the first time. In addition, future research directions and open challenges are identified to stimulate the on-going global debate. Finally, lessons learned to date concerning 6G networks are discussed.

sources.title: 6G for Connected Sky: A Vision for Integrating Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks
sources.abstract: In this paper, we present the vision of our project 6G for Connected Sky (6G-SKY) to integrate terrestrial networks (TNs) and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) and outline the current research activities in 6G research projects in comparison with our project. From the perspectives of industry and academia, we identify key use case segments connecting both aerial and ground users with our 6G-SKY multi-layer network architecture. We explain functional views of our holistic 6G-SKY architecture addressing the heterogeneity of aerial and space platforms. Architecture elements and communication links are identified. We discuss 6G-SKY network design and management functionalities by considering a set of inherent challenges posed by the multi-layer 3-dimensional networks, which we termed as combined airspace and NTN (combined ASN). Finally, we investigate additional research challenges for 6G-SKY project targets.

sources.title: 6G Takes Shape
sources.venue: IEEE BITS the Information Theory Magazine
sources.abstract: The contoursof 6G—its key technical components and driving requirements—are finally coming into focus. Through 20 questions and answers, this article defines the important aspects of 6G across four categories. First, we identify the key themes and forces driving the development of 6G, and what will make 6G unique. We argue that 6G requirements andsystem design will be driven by: first, the tenacious pursuit of spectral (bits/Hz/area), energy (bits/Joule), and cost (bits/dollar) efficiencies, and second, three new service enhancements: sensing/localization/awareness, compute, and global broadband/emergency connectivity. Second, we overview the important role of spectrum in 6G, what new spectrum to expect in 6G, and outline how the different bands will be used to provide 6G services. Third, we focus our attention on the 6G physical layer, including waveforms, MIMO advancements, and the potential use of deep learning. Finally, we explore how global connectivity will be achieved in 6G, through nonterrestrial networks as well as low-cost network expansion via disaggregation and open radio access network. Although 6G standardization activities will not begin until late 2025, meaning this article is by definition speculative, our predictions are informed by several years of intensive research and discussions. Our goal is to provide a grounded perspective that will be helpful to both researchers and engineers as we move into the 6G era.

sources.title: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing (AFDM) for 6G: Properties, Features, and Challenges
sources.abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is an emerging waveform candidate for future sixth generation (6G) systems offering a range of promising features, such as enhanced robustness in heterogeneous and high-mobility environments, as well as inherent suitability for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) applications. In addition, unlike other candidates such as orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) modulation, AFDM provides several unique advantages that strengthen its relevance to practical deployment and standardization in 6G. Notably, as a natural generalization of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), strong backward compatibility with existing conventional systems is guaranteed, while also offering novel possibilities in waveform design, for example to enable physical-layer security through its inherent chirp parametrization. In all, this article provides an overview of AFDM, emphasizing its suitability as a candidate waveform for 6G standardization. First, we provide a concise introduction to the fundamental properties and unique characteristics of AFDM, followed by highlights of its advantageous features, and finally a discussion of its potential and challenges in 6G standardization efforts and representative requirements.

sources.title: 6G: The Intelligent Network of Everything
sources.abstract: The global 6G vision has taken its shape after years of international research and development efforts. This work culminated in ITU-R Recommendation on “IMT-2030 Framework”. While the definition phase of technological requirements is currently ongoing, 3GPP standardization process on 6G networks is expected to start in 2025 and worldwide commercialization around 2029–2030. It is timely to present an up-to-date overview of the entire 6G research field. This article serves as a comprehensive guide to 6G by providing an overall vision, a contemporary survey of the main literature, and an informative tutorial-type presentation style. In our vision, 6G will be based on three fundamental elements: wireless, artificial intelligence, and Internet of Everything. Consequently, 6G can ultimately become the Intelligent Network of Everything while serving as an enabling platform for the next major disruption in mobile communication, called mobile intelligence. The potential of mobile intelligence is that anything can be made connected, intelligent, and aware of its environment. This will revolutionize the way how devices, systems, and applications are designed; how they operate and interact with humans and each other; and how they can be used for the benefit of people, society, and the world in general. After high-level visioning, the main details of 6G are discussed, including fundamental elements, disruptive applications, key use cases, main performance requirements, potential technologies, and defining features. A special focus is given to a comprehensive set of potential 6G technologies, each of which is introduced in a tutorial manner, with a discussion on the vision, introduction, past, present, opportunities, challenges, literature, and future research directions. Finally, we speculate on what comes after 6G and sketch the first high-level vision of 7G. All in all, the objective of this article is to provide a thorough guide to 6G in order to serve as a source of knowledge and inspiration for further research and development work in academia, industry, and standardization bodies.

sources.title: Distributed Intelligent Sensing and Communications for 6G: Architecture and Use Cases
sources.abstract: The Distributed Intelligent Sensing and Communication (DISAC) framework redefines Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) for 6G by leveraging distributed architectures to enhance scalability, adaptability, and resource efficiency. This paper presents key architectural enablers, including advanced data representation, seamless target handover, support for heterogeneous devices, and semantic integration. Two use cases illustrate the transformative potential of DISAC: smart factory shop floors and Vulnerable Road User (VRU) protection at smart intersections. These scenarios demonstrate significant improvements in precision, safety, and operational efficiency compared to traditional ISAC systems. The preliminary DISAC architecture incorporates intelligent data processing, distributed coordination, and emerging technologies such as Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) to meet 6G's stringent requirements. By addressing critical challenges in sensing accuracy, latency, and real-time decision-making, DISAC positions itself as a cornerstone for next-generation wireless networks, advancing innovation in dynamic and complex environments.

sources.title: Toward immersive communications in 6G
sources.abstract: The sixth generation (6G) networks are expected to enable immersive communications and bridge the physical and the virtual worlds. Integrating extended reality, holography, and haptics, immersive communications will revolutionize how people work, entertain, and communicate by enabling lifelike interactions. However, the unprecedented demand for data transmission rate and the stringent requirements on latency and reliability create challenges for 6G networks to support immersive communications. In this survey article, we present the prospect of immersive communications and investigate emerging solutions to the corresponding challenges for 6G. First, we introduce use cases of immersive communications, in the fields of entertainment, education, and healthcare. Second, we present the concepts of immersive communications, including extended reality, haptic communication, and holographic communication, their basic implementation procedures, and their requirements on networks in terms of transmission rate, latency, and reliability. Third, we summarize the potential solutions to addressing the challenges from the aspects of communication, computing, and networking. Finally, we discuss future research directions and conclude this study.

sources.title: End-to-End O-RAN Testbed for Edge-AI-Enabled 5G/6G Connected Industrial Robotics
sources.abstract: Connected robotics is one of the principal use cases driving the transition towards more intelligent and capable 6G mobile cellular networks. Replacing wired connections with highly reliable, high-throughput, and low-latency 5G/6G radio interfaces enables robotic system mobility and the offloading of compute-intensive artificial intelligence (AI) models for robotic perception and control to servers located at the network edge. The transition towards Edge AI as a Service (E-AIaaS) simplifies on-site maintenance of robotic systems and reduces operational costs in industrial environments, while supporting flexible AI model life-cycle management and seamless upgrades of robotic functionalities over time. In this paper, we present a 5G/6G O-RAN-based end-to-end testbed that integrates E-AIaaS for connected industrial robotic applications. The objective is to design and deploy a generic experimental platform based on open technologies and interfaces, demonstrated through an E-AIaaS-enabled autonomous welding scenario. Within this scenario, the testbed is used to investigate trade-offs among different data acquisition, edge processing, and real-time streaming approaches for robotic perception, while supporting emerging paradigms such as semantic and goal-oriented communications.

sources.title: Goal-Oriented and Semantic Communication in 6G AI-Native Networks: The 6G-GOALS Approach
sources.venue: Joint European Conference on Networks and Communications & 6G Summit (EuCNC/6G Summit)
sources.abstract: Recent advances in AI technologies have notably expanded device intelligence, fostering federation and cooperation among distributed AI agents. These advancements impose new requirements on future 6G mobile network architectures. To meet these demands, it is essential to transcend classical boundaries and integrate communication, computation, control, and intelligence. This paper presents the 6G-GOALS approach to goal-oriented and semantic communications for AI-Native 6G Networks. The proposed approach incorporates semantic, pragmatic, and goal-oriented communication into AI-native technologies, aiming to facilitate information exchange between intelligent agents in a more relevant, effective, and timely manner, thereby optimizing bandwidth, latency, energy, and electromagnetic field (EMF) radiation. The focus is on distilling data to its most relevant form and terse representation, aligning with the source’s intent or the destination’s objectives and context, or serving a specific goal. 6G-GOALS builds on three fundamental pillars: i) AI-enhanced semantic data representation, sensing, compression, and communication, ii) foundational AI reasoning and causal semantic data representation, contextual relevance, and value for goal-oriented effectiveness, and iii) sustainability enabled by more efficient wireless services. Finally, we illustrate two proof-of-concepts implementing semantic, goal-oriented, and pragmatic communication principles in near-future use cases. Our study covers the project’s vision, methodologies, and potential impact.

sources.title: Towards 6G Intelligence: The Role of Generative AI in Future Wireless Networks
sources.abstract: Ambient intelligence (AmI) is a computing paradigm in which physical environments are embedded with sensing, computation, and communication so they can perceive people and context, decide appropriate actions, and respond autonomously. Realizing AmI at global scale requires sixth generation (6G) wireless networks with capabilities for real time perception, reasoning, and action aligned with human behavior and mobility patterns. We argue that Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is the creative core of such environments. Unlike traditional AI, GenAI learns data distributions and can generate realistic samples, making it well suited to close key AmI gaps, including generating synthetic sensor and channel data in under observed areas, translating user intent into compact, semantic messages, predicting future network conditions for proactive control, and updating digital twins without compromising privacy. This chapter reviews foundational GenAI models, GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, and generative transformers, and connects them to practical AmI use cases, including spectrum sharing, ultra reliable low latency communication, intelligent security, and context aware digital twins. We also examine how 6G enablers, such as edge and fog computing, IoT device swarms, intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS), and non terrestrial networks, can host or accelerate distributed GenAI. Finally, we outline open challenges in energy efficient on device training, trustworthy synthetic data, federated generative learning, and AmI specific standardization. We show that GenAI is not a peripheral addition, but a foundational element for transforming 6G from a faster network into an ambient intelligent ecosystem.

sources.title: 6G Enabled Advanced Transportation Systems
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
sources.abstract: With the emergence of communication services with stringent requirements such as autonomous driving or on-flight Internet, the sixth-generation (6G) wireless network is envisaged to become an enabling technology for future transportation systems. In this paper, two ways of interactions between 6G networks and transportation are extensively investigated. On one hand, the new usage scenarios and capabilities of 6G over existing cellular networks are firstly highlighted. Then, its potential in seamless and ubiquitous connectivity across the heterogeneous space-air-ground transportation systems is demonstrated, where railways, airplanes, high-altitude platforms and satellites are investigated. On the other hand, we reveal that the introduction of 6G guarantees a more intelligent, efficient and secure transportation system. Specifically, technical analysis on how 6G can empower future transportation is provided, based on the latest research and standardization progresses in localization, integrated sensing and communications, and security. The technical challenges and insights for a road ahead are also summarized for possible inspirations on 6G enabled advanced transportation.

sources.title: Dynamic Authorization for Knowledge-Base Agents in 6G
sources.abstract: As 6G architectures transition toward decentralized Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), ensuring secure access to shared Knowledge Bases (KB) is critical. Traditional authorization models like RBAC fail to provide the granularity required for autonomous agents interacting with Semantic-based data. This work proposes a hybrid authorization framework that integrates roles and First-Order Logic (FOL) predicates to enforce zero-trust principles at the knowledge-graph level. We eliminate permission inheritance by enforcing authorization at the triple level (Subject-Predicate-Object), ensuring agents only access metadata required for their specific functional lifecycle.

sources.title: Security and Privacy on 6G Network Edge: A Survey
sources.abstract: To meet the stringent service requirements of 6G applications such as immersive cloud eXtended Reality (XR), holographic communication, and digital twin, there is no doubt that an increasing number of servers will be deployed on the network edge. Then, the techniques, edge computing, edge caching, and edge intelligence will be more widely utilized for intelligent local data storage and processing generated by 6G applications, while innovative access network architecture based on the cloud-edge servers, such as the Open-Radio Access Network (O-RAN) will be adopted to improve the flexibility and openness for new service deployment and frequent network changes. On the other hand, new attack surfaces and vectors targeting local infrastructure and users will emerge along with the deployment of novel network architecture and techniques. Massive researchers have studied the potential security and privacy threats on the 6G network edge as well as the countermeasures. The three techniques, edge computing, edge caching, and edge intelligence have become a double-edged sword that can not only be synchronously utilized to develop defense countermeasures, but also become the targets of many new security and privacy threats. In this article, we provide a comprehensive survey of articles on the three techniques-related security threats and countermeasures on the 6G network edge. We explain how security and privacy can be destroyed by attacking one of the three technologies and how the three services support each other to realize efficient and achievable security protection. Moreover, the researches on the benefits and limitations of Federated Learning (FL) and blockchain for decentralized edge network systems in terms of security and privacy are also investigated. Additionally, we also analyze the existing challenges and future directions towards 6G.

sources.title: Wireless Network Digital Twin for 6G: Generative AI as A Key Enabler
sources.abstract: Digital twin, which enables emulation, evaluation, and optimization of physical entities through synchronized digital replicas, has gained increasing attention as a promising technology for intricate wireless networks. For 6G, numerous innovative wireless technologies and network architectures have posed new challenges in establishing wireless network digital twins. To tackle these challenges, artificial intelligence (AI), particularly the flourishing generative AI, emerges as a potential solution. In this article, we discuss emerging prerequisites for wireless network digital twins considering the complicated network architecture, tremendous network scale, extensive coverage, and diversified application scenarios in the 6G era. We further explore the applications of generative AI, such as Transformer and diffusion model, to empower the 6G digital twin from multiple perspectives including physical-digital modeling, synchronization, and slicing capability. Subsequently, we propose a hierarchical generative AI-enabled wireless network digital twin at both the message-level and policy-level, and provide a typical use case with numerical results to validate the effectiveness and efficiency. Finally, open research issues for wireless network digital twins in the 6G era are discussed.

findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Direct statement in the abstract of a peer-reviewed IEEE Access survey. Commercialization timing is the paper's expectation, not an observed outcome.

findings.claim: 6G system design is framed as being driven by continued spectral, energy and cost efficiency gains plus three new service classes: sensing/localization/awareness, compute, and global broadband/emergency connectivity.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Verbatim from the abstract of an IEEE Information Theory Magazine article; the article itself labels its predictions speculative because standardization had not begun at writing.
findings.supporting_excerpt: 6G requirements andsystem design will be driven by: first, the tenacious pursuit of spectral (bits/Hz/area), energy (bits/Joule), and cost (bits/dollar) efficiencies, and second, three new service enhancements: sensing/localization/awareness, compute, and global broadband/emergency connectivity.

findings.claim: Full integration of non-terrestrial components (satellites, high-altitude platforms, aerial users) into 6G, and the terrestrial/non-terrestrial convergence it requires, is a recurring architectural pillar across the retrieved literature.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Five abstracts independently treat terrestrial/non-terrestrial integration as central: NTN RAT challenges and waveform/RRM co-design, a multi-layer 3D architecture for aerial and ground users, NTN as the route to global connectivity, space-air-ground transportation connectivity, and NTNs as hosts for distributed generative AI. Two of these supporting items are arXiv preprints and not peer reviewed.

findings.claim: AI-native design is presented as a defining property of 6G, with semantic and goal-oriented communication proposed to replace or augment bit-centric transport by exchanging distilled, task-relevant representations between intelligent agents.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The 6G-GOALS paper frames semantic/pragmatic/goal-oriented communication as an AI-native architecture pillar with bandwidth, latency, energy and EMF motivations; the 'Intelligent Network of Everything' survey lists AI as one of three fundamental 6G elements; the GenAI/ambient-intelligence chapter argues GenAI can translate user intent into compact semantic messages and generate synthetic channel data; DISAC adds semantic integration to sensing. Multiple independent groups align on the concept, but the abstracts report limited quantitative validation.

findings.claim: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is advanced as a 6G waveform candidate distinguished by backward compatibility with OFDM and by chirp-parameter-based physical-layer security.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Single arXiv preprint (2025, eess.SP) that is explicitly an overview arguing for AFDM's suitability in 6G standardization; no independent measurement or comparative result is reported in the abstract.
findings.supporting_excerpt: strong backward compatibility with existing conventional systems is guaranteed, while also offering novel possibilities in waveform design, for example to enable physical-layer security through its inherent chirp parametrization.

findings.claim: Integrated sensing and communication in 6G is being extended from co-located designs toward distributed architectures (DISAC), with stated gains claimed for precision, safety and operational efficiency in factory and vulnerable-road-user scenarios.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Abstract-only evidence from one arXiv preprint (eess.SP, April 2025); the claimed improvements are stated qualitatively without figures in the abstract. A separate survey confirms ISAC is a recognized 6G element for transportation, which strengthens the direction but not the DISAC-specific claim.
findings.supporting_excerpt: The Distributed Intelligent Sensing and Communication (DISAC) framework redefines Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) for 6G by leveraging distributed architectures to enhance scalability, adaptability, and resource efficiency.

findings.claim: Immersive communication (extended reality, haptics, holography) is the 6G use-case cluster most consistently used to justify extreme rate, latency and reliability targets.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The immersive-communications survey states such services demand unprecedented transmission rate and stringent latency/reliability; the operator perspective and the edge-security survey both use XR, holograms and digital twins as the motivating 6G applications. These are requirement claims from surveys, not demonstrated deployments.

findings.claim: Edge infrastructure (edge computing, caching, edge intelligence) and O-RAN openness are treated as prerequisites for 6G services, and simultaneously as expanding the security attack surface, motivating zero-trust and fine-grained authorization work.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The edge-security survey explicitly frames edge computing/caching/intelligence as a 'double-edged sword' enabling defence but creating new threats; the 2026 arXiv preprint proposes triple-level (Subject-Predicate-Object) authorization with FOL predicates for multi-agent knowledge bases in 6G, and the O-RAN testbed paper shows edge offloading for industrial robotics. The authorization proposal is a single unreviewed preprint.

findings.claim: Generative AI (transformers, diffusion models, GANs, VAEs) is being positioned as a key enabler for wireless network digital twins and for synthesizing sensor, channel and semantic data in 6G.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Three abstracts converge: a hierarchical generative-AI wireless digital twin with a numerical use case (arXiv preprint), a GenAI-for-ambient-intelligence review covering synthetic sensor/channel data and digital-twin updating with privacy constraints, and the 6G survey's AI-centric vision. The digital-twin evidence remains largely architectural; only one abstract mentions numerical validation.

findings.claim: Testbeds and experimental platforms for 6G-era services are now appearing, including an end-to-end O-RAN testbed for edge-AI-enabled industrial robotics and a survey-level catalogue of 6G verification platforms.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The O-RAN robotics testbed is an arXiv preprint (cs.RO, 2026) describing an experimental platform and its trade-offs; the 2023 IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials article presents testbeds and advanced 6G verification platforms. Neither abstract reports commercial deployment.
findings.supporting_excerpt: we present a 5G/6G O-RAN-based end-to-end testbed that integrates E-AIaaS for connected industrial robotic applications.

findings.claim: Consensus on 6G's defining services is explicitly lacking: surveys and operator analyses flag that unique 'killer services' and innovative device form factors remain unidentified.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The operator-perspective article states the gap directly; the large 6G survey notes global discussions remain wide open with numerous open issues; the Information Theory Magazine overview calls its own 6G predictions by definition speculative.
findings.supporting_excerpt: However, the identification of “killer services” unique to 6G and the development of innovative form factor devices are deemed crucial for delivering unprecedented customer experiences.

findings.claim: Spectrum strategy for 6G is framed as two-track: exploring new high-frequency candidate bands while refarming under-utilised spectrum in existing services.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Stated in an IEEE Communications Magazine article from an operator perspective; the same article reports measurement results for high-frequency candidate bands, but only the abstract was available here.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Notably, simultaneous exploration of new spectrum and refarming of underutilized spec-trum in existing services are highlighted as imperative.

limitations: All conclusions are drawn from titles and abstracts only; no full paper was read and no underlying results, figures or proofs were inspected.
Sample is small (16 items) and dominated by surveys, vision/position papers and magazine overviews rather than experimental studies.

Several retrieved items are arXiv preprints and have not been peer reviewed; conclusions that rest on them (AFDM, DISAC, edge-AI robotics testbed, GenAI digital twins, 6G multi-agent authorization) are correspondingly weaker.
Commercialization and standardization dates are paper-stated expectations, and the 6G service/timeline landscape is explicitly described as not yet settled.
No paper here provides evidence of commercial success, deployment scale or investment outcome, and none is used to claim any.
Coverage is skewed to network architecture, sensing, security and AI topics; coverage of device hardware, silicon and energy-efficiency metrics is thin.
Publication years span 2023–2026, so older surveys may not reflect the most recent standardization state.

sources.title: Quantum Fuzzy Decision Systems for Cognitive Radio-Based Spectrum Allocation in 6G Networks
sources.venue: International Conference on Intelligent Innovations in Engineering and Technology (ICIIET)
sources.abstract: Quantum Fuzzy Decision Systems Cognitive Radio-Based Spectrum Allocation in 6G Networks covers the growing demand of smart, adaptive, and more efficient spectrum control in the future wireless world. As 6G promises to be a massive connectivity option, cognitive radio should transform to manage a rapid spectrum variation, saturation of users, and varied quality-of-service (QoS) requirements. Conventional spectrum allocation methods tend to have high uncertainty, low real time flexibility, and slow decision making due to either traditional optimization or rule-based systems. These drawbacks result in an inefficient use, augmented interference and deteriorated network performance in dynamic 6G surroundings. In order to address these problems, the paper presents Quantum-Enhanced Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision Optimization (QF-MCDO) framework. The approach combines quantum state encoding and fuzzy inversion to consider a set of spectrum parameters at once, which can make decisions more quickly and with more uncertainty, as well as use channels more efficiently. Quantum superposition is used to improve the search process and fuzzy logic improves the interpretability and robustness. The real-time intelligent spectrum sharing on the massive-IoT-based 6G environment is implemented using the proposed system and guarantees adaptive channel selection when dealing with dense and unpredictable traffic patterns. It has been experimentally demonstrated that, QF-MCDO has a much better allocation accuracy, lesser decision-latency, lesser interference and greater overall spectrum-efficiency than classical use of cognitive radio approaches. The proposed method achieves the allocation accuracy improvement by 80%, reduced latency$(30 ~\text{ms})$, interference minimization$(-80 \text{dBm})$, enhanced spectrum efficiency of 6Hz.

sources.title: DEEP LEARNING-BASED SPECTRUM SENSING AND DYNAMIC SPECTRUM ALLOCATION FOR 6G NETWORKS
sources.abstract: The rapid growth of immersive applications, massive Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, intelligent transportation, and ultra-reliable services in 6G networks increases demand for radio spectrum. Conventional static allocation cannot adequately utilize spectrum that remains temporarily unused, while conventional sensing techniques experience performance degradation under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), noise uncertainty, fading, and rapidly changing channel conditions. Recent studies indicate that deep learning can improve spectrum sensing by learning discriminative signal characteristics directly from received observations. Existing approaches generally address spectrum sensing and spectrum allocation as separate tasks, which can limit their responsiveness to instantaneous spectrum occupancy and traffic conditions. This study proposes a novel Deep Adaptive Spectrum Sensing and Allocation Network (DASSAN) that integrates a CNN-BiLSTM feature-learning module with an attention mechanism for spectrum occupancy detection and a deep reinforcement learning allocator for dynamic channel selection. The CNN extracts local spectral features, while BiLSTM captures temporal channel occupancy patterns. The attention mechanism emphasizes informative features, and the reinforcement-learning agent jointly considers spectrum availability, interference, traffic demand, and channel quality to select allocation decisions. The integrated framework is designed to improve sensing reliability, spectrum utilization, throughput, and allocation adaptability in dynamic 6G environments. The simulated results show that DASSAN achieves 99.1% accuracy, 99.3% detection probability, 3.4% false alarm rate, 128.3 Mbps throughput, and 95.8% spectrum utilization at 20 dB SNR. At 0 dB, it achieves 93.1% accuracy, 95.1% detection probability, 6.4% false alarm rate, 71.9 Mbps throughput, and 83.9% spectrum utilization. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating deep spectrum sensing with adaptive reinforcement-learning-based allocation for dynamic 6G environments.

sources.title: Towards 6G V2X Sidelink: Survey of Resource Allocation—Mathematical Formulations, Challenges, and Proposed Solutions
sources.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
sources.abstract: The advent of 6G marks a transformative phase in wireless communication, ushering in a hyperconnected experience. This paper explores optimizing sidelink technologies in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication through integrating 6G capabilities. Emphasizing challenges in sidelink resource allocation, the study introduces mathematical solutions. The survey further investigates the evolution of Cellular-V2X (C-V2X) and sidelink standardization within the 6G V2X Sidelink context, highlighting key features and applications. Additionally, it examines inter-UE coordination, resource re-evaluation, and pre-emption operations in 5G-V2X Sidelink, addressing associated challenges and mathematical formulations. The paper focuses on power-based resource allocation in 5G-V2X, addressing challenges and proposing solutions for the 6G V2X Sidelink landscape. Encompassing direct communication, collision issues, spectrum compliance, resource fairness, uncertainty, and interference management, the survey comprehensively explores challenges and solutions in current sidelink resource allocation. It evaluates traditional and emerging techniques, such as cognitive radio, cooperative communication, power control, dynamic spectrum access, ML-aided allocation, blockchain-enabled allocation, and edge computing-driven allocation. The resource allocation requirements for diverse V2X services in 6G V2X Sidelink are outlined, explicitly focusing on Vehicular to Vehicular (V2V), Vehicular to Infrastructure (V2I), Vehicular to Pedestrian (V2P), and other V2X services, addressing their specific needs.

sources.title: Joint spectrum allocation and power control for D2D communication and sensing in 6G networks using DRL-based hyper-heuristics
Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Spectrum Allocation in 6G Networks
sources.abstract: In this paper, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework is proposed for opportunistic spectrum access in cognitive radio networks (CRNs). The proposed framework consists of cooperative sensing, adaptive policy optimization, and distributed coordination for dynamic, efficient, and interpretable spectrum utilization. It is trained with diverse datasets from simulated and real environments to enhance generalization across spectral loads and interference levels. Experimental results show that the developed framework achieves a maximum throughput of 31.1 Mbps, an average fairness index of 0.95, and a latency reduction of <5 ms compared with conventional agents. Cross-dataset evaluation verifies accuracy over 95%, throughput retention over 96%, and a loss of <3% when transferring between synthetic and real data domains. Robustness testing revealed an accuracy change of <4.5% under −5 dB signal to noise ratio and a minimal throughput loss of 7.5%. Computational scalability remains stable as the number of agents increases, and interpretability analysis shows consistent policy behavior with entropy between 0.69 and 0.75. These results validate the developed framework as a reliable, scalable, and explainable basis for adaptive and autonomous cognitive radio systems.

sources.title: 6G Takes Shape
sources.venue: IEEE BITS the Information Theory Magazine
sources.abstract: The contoursof 6G—its key technical components and driving requirements—are finally coming into focus. Through 20 questions and answers, this article defines the important aspects of 6G across four categories. First, we identify the key themes and forces driving the development of 6G, and what will make 6G unique. We argue that 6G requirements andsystem design will be driven by: first, the tenacious pursuit of spectral (bits/Hz/area), energy (bits/Joule), and cost (bits/dollar) efficiencies, and second, three new service enhancements: sensing/localization/awareness, compute, and global broadband/emergency connectivity. Second, we overview the important role of spectrum in 6G, what new spectrum to expect in 6G, and outline how the different bands will be used to provide 6G services. Third, we focus our attention on the 6G physical layer, including waveforms, MIMO advancements, and the potential use of deep learning. Finally, we explore how global connectivity will be achieved in 6G, through nonterrestrial networks as well as low-cost network expansion via disaggregation and open radio access network. Although 6G standardization activities will not begin until late 2025, meaning this article is by definition speculative, our predictions are informed by several years of intensive research and discussions. Our goal is to provide a grounded perspective that will be helpful to both researchers and engineers as we move into the 6G era.

sources.title: A Novel Fuzzy-based Spectrum Allocation (FBSA) Technique for Enhanced Quality of Service (QoS) in 6G Heterogeneous Networks
sources.venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
sources.abstract: This research focuses on Device to Any device (D2A) communication for 6G in unpredictable circumstances where the topology of the D2A network changes over time as a result of the mobility of D2A Devices. Extremely sophisticated applications with demands for ultra-low latency and ultra-high data rate can be made achievable by cellular D2A communications in 6G. The best way to ensure Quality of Service (QoS) is to make the most of the scarce MAC Layer resources. To share information between D2A systems and a variety of devices, spectrum allocation is crucial. In this paper, a novel Fuzzy Based Spectrum Allocation (FBSA) approach is established to efficiently and rational distribute resources for D2A. A system model for D2A transmission has been established for metropolitan regions, common security and non-secure services are implemented in the network to assess the network performance for this feasible technique. Comparing the proposed FBSA approach to its prior works, which could not deliver guaranteed services due to low resource utilization. Riverbed Modeler simulation results show that the proposed approach can significantly enhance resource usage and satisfy the requirements of D2A systems.

sources.title: Resource allocation scheme for eMBB and uRLLC coexistence in 6G networks
sources.abstract: Abstract 5G technology is intended to support three promising services with heterogeneous requirements: Ultra-Reliable and Low Latency Communication (uRLLC), enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), and massive Machine Type Communication (mMTC). 6G is required to support even more challenging scenarios, including the presence of a large number of uRLLC devices, under the massive uRLLC (mURLLC) use case scenario. The presence of these services on the same network creates a challenging task of resource allocation to meet their diverse requirements. Given the critical nature of uRLLC applications, uRLLC traffic will always have the highest priority which causes a negative impact on the performance of other services. In this paper, the problem of uRLLC/eMBB resource allocation is investigated. An optimal resource allocation scheme is proposed with two scenarios including a guaranteed fairness level and minimum data rate among eMBB users. In addition, a knapsack-inspired punctured resource allocation algorithm is proposed where the users’ channel qualities of both services are considered at each time slot leading to the most suitable Resource Block (RB) selection for puncturing in a way that minimizes the negative impact on eMBB performance. The proposed solution was compared with three puncturing baseline reference algorithms and the performance was evaluated in terms of eMBB Sum throughput and Fairness level. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the above-mentioned reference algorithms in all evaluation metrics and is proved to be comparable to the optimal solution given its low complexity.

sources.title: On Spectral Intelligence in 6G URLLC Networks
sources.abstract: Cognitive radio (CR)-empowered 6G networks are deemed a key candidate technology to achieve ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) with enhanced spectrum utilization efficiency. However, there are several challenges to address in achieving this objective. In particular, the sequential and random sensing performed by secondary users (SUs) to find idle channels within a given band in a CR network (CRN) leads to time and energy consumption, and processing overheads, which consequently cause early depletion of the device's energy, underutilization of the available spectrum, and prolonged delays in communication. To circumvent this problem, in this paper, a spectrum efficient scheme is proposed based on idle spectrum inference and ranking, which takes into account the devices' heterogeneity as well as their priorities in resource allocation. Based on the probabilistic approach, the scheme uses multiple parameters in a channel's evaluation and suitability assessment before selection for transmission. Markov chain modeling is leveraged to deal with the users' arrival and departure uncertainties and to derive expressions for core performance metrics, including service capacity and retainability, spectrum utilization efficiency, reliability, network unserviceable and handoff probabilities, channel availability, and communication latency. The scheme is analyzed under various patterns of users' arrivals. The acquired analytical and simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme compared to the state-of-the-art to realize URLLC applications.

sources.title: The Synergy of Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain in 6G Spectrum Management
sources.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligences real-time data analysis abilities can be used to empower dynamic spectrum allocation and interference alleviation, adjusting dynamically to shifting user needs and environmental conditions. Meanwhile, Blockchain technology, with its decentralized ledger and smart contracts can be used to ensure secure, transparent, and efficient spectrum allocation while protecting against unauthorized access and interference. This chapter highlights the transformative potential of AI and blockchain in optimizing 6G spectrum management, powering seamless connectivity, and confirming the reliability of future wireless communication systems.

sources.title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
sources.abstract: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.

findings.claim: Mid-band spectrum for 6G is largely already allocated to incumbents, so access depends on coexistence with satellite and radar services. This is a regulatory and technical constraint on 6G capacity, not just an optimization problem.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Rests on a single arXiv preprint, which is not peer reviewed. The abstract proposes four techniques but gives no quantitative performance or field results, so it is unclear how well they protect incumbents in practice.
findings.supporting_excerpt: With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G.

findings.claim: Much of the 6G spectrum-allocation evidence appears to come from simulation or analytical models (Riverbed Modeler, Markov-chain analysis, puncturing simulations). Abstracts show no hardware testbeds or field trials, so real-world transferability is unproven.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstracts state simulation or analytical validation (e.g. 'Riverbed Modeler simulation results', 'simulation results show', 'analytical and simulation results'). Absence of mention of testbeds in an abstract is a gap, not proof that none exist. Several of these are low-citation papers in smaller venues.

findings.claim: Cognitive-radio sensing has overheads and weak spots. Sequential sensing costs time and device energy, and conventional sensing degrades at low SNR, under noise uncertainty and in fading. This limits how much of the claimed spectrum-efficiency gain survives in practice, especially for battery-limited IoT devices.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Two abstracts describe the problem directly. A third reports a 7.5% throughput loss and a <4.5% accuracy change at -5 dB SNR for a proposed RL framework, so robustness is reduced but not eliminated. The proposed fixes are mostly evaluated by their own authors.
findings.supporting_excerpt: leads to time and energy consumption, and processing overheads, which consequently cause early depletion of the device's energy

findings.claim: Some papers use deep reinforcement learning or deep-learning allocators, but their abstracts leave out compute cost, training-data provenance, inference latency on real base-station or device hardware, and behaviour under distribution shift. The reported gains cannot be judged for deployability.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: src_685884e0e9 claims cross-dataset transfer 'between synthetic and real data domains' but does not describe the real data. The reported 31.1 Mbps peak throughput is not placed against 6G targets in the abstract. The src_1a88a65962 abstract is truncated before any results. src_62856d3286 has metadata only. This is a gap in the evidence, not a demonstrated failure.

findings.claim: The quantum-enhanced fuzzy spectrum-allocation framework is weakly evidenced. The abstract does not say whether it runs on quantum hardware or is a classical simulation inspired by quantum ideas, and its performance claims are cut off before any numbers appear.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Single conference abstract with 0 citations. It says it uses 'quantum superposition' to improve search, but the abstract does not specify a hardware platform, and the 'experimentally demonstrated' claim is truncated. Any quantum advantage for 6G spectrum control should be treated as unproven.

findings.claim: Meeting uRLLC requirements structurally degrades other services. Prioritizing uRLLC traffic harms eMBB performance, and the proposed puncturing algorithms only mitigate this trade-off rather than remove it, which matters as 6G targets massive uRLLC deployments.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The abstract states the trade-off directly. The mitigation is shown by simulation against three baseline puncturing algorithms, not against deployed systems. The paper starts from 5G service classes and extends them to 6G.
findings.supporting_excerpt: uRLLC traffic will always have the highest priority which causes a negative impact on the performance of other services.

findings.claim: Much '6G' literature builds on 5G mechanisms and is explicitly speculative about the standard. The 6G label may therefore overstate how much is 6G-specific, and requirements may shift once standardization matures.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The survey 'Towards 6G V2X Sidelink' examines 5G-V2X mechanisms. 'On 6G Takes Shape' says it is speculative and was written before standardization began. The eMBB/uRLLC paper builds on 5G service categories. The abstracts do not show the current state of 3GPP work as of November 2026.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Although 6G standardization activities will not begin until late 2025, meaning this article is by definition speculative

findings.claim: The AI-plus-blockchain case for 6G spectrum management has no quantitative support in the retrieved material. Blockchain overheads (latency, throughput, energy) in real-time spectrum sharing are not addressed.
findings.label: unverified_claim
findings.rationale: The book-chapter abstract is conceptual and uses promotional language ('transformative potential') with no data. The absence of overhead analysis is a gap, not evidence that overhead is prohibitive.

hype_flags: 'Transformative potential' of AI and blockchain in 6G spectrum management: conceptual, with no data or overhead analysis (src_935e6ca0aa).
Quantum superposition for 6G spectrum allocation: no hardware platform or advantage evidence is visible in the abstract (src_69c822a150).
'Reliable, scalable, and explainable' RL spectrum access: validated on simulated and unspecified 'real' datasets, and the 31.1 Mbps throughput is not put in context (src_685884e0e9).
Many papers claim large allocation or QoS gains over baselines chosen by the authors, using simulation only (src_c2da58e411, src_4a927e0181).
Labeling 5G-derived techniques as '6G' without 6G-specific validation (src_aeb86924e4, src_4a927e0181).

finding.claim: S1 presents an expectation as a verified, high-confidence fact. The cited abstract says 3GPP work is 'expected' to start in 2025 and commercialization is expected around 2029–2030. These are forecasts from one article. Another retrieved paper says standardization will not begin until late 2025 and calls itself speculative. Operator analyses put 6G only 'around 2030'. The timeline should be labelled a forecast with a stated uncertainty range.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The quoted wording is forward-looking. src_05afb24a42 says 'standardization activities will not begin until late 2025, meaning this article is by definition speculative', which conflicts mildly with a flat 2025 start. A dated schedule is a forecast, not a verified fact.
finding.supporting_excerpt: 3GPP standardization process on 6G networks is expected to start in 2025 and worldwide commercialization around 2029–2030.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S2 reports the three new service classes and the efficiency drivers as the framing of 6G system design. The cited abstract is an author position piece ('We argue...') that calls itself speculative. It is not a consensus or standards statement, and 'verified_fact | high' overstates its weight. S11 says consensus on 6G's defining services is lacking, and S7 names immersive communication as the main justification for 6G targets. Neither fits well with S2's three-service framing.
finding.label: unverified_claim
finding.rationale: 'We argue' marks an authors' thesis, not an agreed framing. The finding should say whose framing it is and note the tension with S7 and S11.
finding.supporting_excerpt: We argue that 6G requirements and system design will be driven by: first, the tenacious pursuit of spectral (bits/Hz/area), energy (bits/Joule), and cost (bits/dollar) efficiencies
finding.guard_note: downgraded from verified_fact: supporting excerpt missing or not found in the cited source text

finding.claim: S3 calls NTN integration a recurring architectural pillar but omits the main caveat in its own cited sources. The NTN overview says integration 'brings forth a set of its own challenges' in radio access, resource management, spectral coexistence and waveform design. The cited papers are largely preprints and project visions (6G-SKY), not validated designs. The finding reads as settled convergence when the abstracts describe open problems.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstracts frame NTN integration as a vision with unresolved RAT challenges. Frequency of mention across papers is not evidence of feasibility.
finding.supporting_excerpt: However, this integration into 6G brings forth a set of its own challenges, particularly in Radio Access Technologies (RATs).
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S4 says AI-native design is 'presented as a defining property' and that semantic communication is proposed to 'replace or augment' bit-centric transport. The evidence is thin. The strongest source is a single project approach (6G-GOALS) that only 'aims' to facilitate better exchange and offers two proofs-of-concept in 'near-future use cases'. Other cited sources are preprints and vision papers. No abstract shows semantic communication outperforming bit-level transport at scale, and 'replace' goes beyond what they state.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Proofs-of-concept and aims are weak support for calling AI-native or semantic transport a defining property of 6G. The word 'replace' is not supported.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Finally, we illustrate two proof-of-concepts implementing semantic, goal-oriented, and pragmatic communication principles in near-future use cases.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S7 says immersive communication is the use-case cluster 'most consistently' used to justify extreme 6G targets. This is a comparative claim, and the cited abstracts do not support it. The immersive survey covers only its own topic. The operator abstract lists XR and holograms alongside AI, sensing, autonomous vehicles and urban air mobility, and says the unique 'killer services' remain unidentified. src_05afb24a42 names sensing, compute and global connectivity as the new drivers instead. No ranking of use cases is shown.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The retrieved abstracts do not compare use-case clusters. The claim is an unsupported inference and sits in tension with S11 and S2.

finding.claim: S8 treats edge infrastructure and O-RAN as 'prerequisites' for 6G services. The cited abstracts say only that more edge servers are expected to be deployed and that O-RAN 'will be adopted' to improve flexibility. That describes an anticipated trend, not a requirement. The O-RAN source is a single-use-case preprint testbed (industrial welding) for 5G/6G. The security evidence is a survey plus a 2026 preprint on knowledge-base authorization with no evaluation shown in the abstract.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: 'Prerequisite' is stronger than the abstracts' 'will be adopted'. The zero-trust claim rests on proposals rather than demonstrated defences.

finding.claim: S9 positions generative AI as a key enabler of digital twins and data synthesis, but the evidence is promotional and unvalidated at scale. Every cited source is an arXiv preprint. The digital-twin paper offers only 'a typical use case with numerical results'. The GenAI chapter itself lists open challenges in energy-efficient on-device training and trustworthy synthetic data, which S9 leaves out. Synthetic channel and sensor data carries risks of fidelity and privacy leakage.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstracts show proposals and a simulated or numerical use case. They also admit open challenges, so 'key enabler' is a position, not an established result.

finding.claim: S10 says testbeds for '6G-era' services are appearing, but the flagship example is a '5G/6G' O-RAN testbed. It is a single-scenario preprint (autonomous welding) with no 6G-specific radio shown. The survey catalogue covers platforms as of its 2023 date. This is evidence of 5G and O-RAN experimentation with 6G framing, not of 6G-specific validation.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The '5G/6G' label and the single demonstration scenario limit what the testbed shows about 6G readiness.
finding.supporting_excerpt: we present a 5G/6G O-RAN-based end-to-end testbed that integrates E-AIaaS for connected industrial robotic applications.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S12 describes spectrum strategy as new high-frequency bands plus refarming, but omits the main constraint. Most spectrum below 15 GHz is already allocated, so 6G access depends on coexistence with satellite and radar incumbents. The finding therefore understates the regulatory and technical barrier, and the 'two-track' framing sounds more tractable than the sources suggest.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The incumbent-coexistence constraint is a precondition for either spectrum track and should be included.
finding.supporting_excerpt: With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical

limitations: Only 12 papers, nearly all on spectrum allocation and cognitive radio. Other 6G risks such as terahertz hardware, power consumption, RIS, ISAC, cost of deployment, standardization timing, security and supply chain are not covered.
Most papers are abstract-only, and two (src_62856d3286, src_cdb600acd9) are metadata-only, so no findings can rest on them. Several abstracts are truncated before the results.
Many sources are low-citation papers in smaller venues. The arXiv preprint (src_31434848d1) is not peer reviewed.
The retrieved set contains no direct counter-evidence from field trials, so statements about missing testbeds describe the retrieval set only.
No company-level or standards-body information is available, so supplier dependence and the standardization status as of 2026-11 cannot be assessed.
Only titles and abstracts were available, so claims about what the full papers show could not be checked.
Several abstracts are truncated, so omissions I flag may be covered later in the text.
Two retrieved papers have no abstract, so they were not used.
Some metadata look anomalous: src_31434848d1 is dated 2026-11-02 and src_1a88a65962 2026-09-01, which I could not verify.
Challenges to S5, S6 and S11 were not raised: they are hedged or well matched to their abstracts, and S11 is directly supported.
I did not search outside the supplied evidence, so contradicting papers outside this set are not considered.

market.coverage_note: Companies are chosen from the evidence: SEC-listed patent assignees and employers of paper authors found by the Patent and Science agents (14 company name(s) in the patents and papers; 3 matched to the SEC ticker file; the top 3 by patents + papers are read), plus filers whose reports mention the topic. News items are headlines only: the articles were not read. Company size and trend figures (revenue, growth, R&D, net income) come from the SEC's XBRL company-facts data as reported by each company; the size class is by revenue, not market value. Companies marked 'discovered' were found by a full-text search of all SEC filings for the topic phrase only; no patent or paper of theirs was found, they are often small, and a mention in a filing says nothing about their size, role or prospects.

In one embodiment, a method performed by a base station comprises, determining a spatial congruence relationship between a first frequency range (FR) antenna array and a second FR antenna array co-located with the first FR antenna array, determining quasi-co-location (QCL) type information based on the spatial congruence relationship, determining correction information for a spatial difference between the first FR antenna array and the second FR antenna array, and transmitting, to a user equipment (UE), the QCL type information and the correction information.

sources.title: METHOD AND DEVICE FOR SUPPORTING MU PAIRING BY USING AI MODEL IN WIRELESS COMMUNICATION SYSTEM [WO2026230909A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. A method performed by a first network node in a wireless communication system, according to one embodiment of the present disclosure, comprises the steps of: identifying channel information based on a sounding reference signal (SRS) transmitted from a terminal; acquiring first information generated on the basis of the channel information; and transmitting a first message including the first information to a second network node that performs a scheduling operation, wherein the first information includes, on the basis of the channel information, a latent vector for the channel information or a correlation value between terminals generated on the basis of the latent vector, and the first information can be used to support multi-user (MU) pairing.

sources.title: SUB-PRB LEVEL UL PRECODER CYCLING [WO2026230772A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a communication method and system for converging a 5th-Generation (5G) communication system or a 6th-Generation (6G) communication system for supporting higher data rates beyond a 4th-Generation (4G) system. A method of operating a base station (BS) includes receiving, from a user equipment (UE), a UE capability report indicating an antenna configuration of the UE, and transmitting, to the UE, a first message including a physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) antenna port and precoder configuration for the UE. The method also includes transmitting, to the UE, a second message including uplink (UL) scheduling information and precoder cycling properties for the UE, and receiving, from the UE, at least one PUSCH transmission based on (i) the PUSCH antenna port and precoder configuration, (ii) the UL scheduling information, and (iii) the precoder cycling properties.

sources.title: DATA COLLECTION CONFIGURATION AND REPORTING METHOD AT BASE STATION [WO2026230951A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a data transmission rate higher than that of a 4G communication system such as LTE. According to one embodiment of the present disclosure, a method performed by a base station in a communication system may be provided. The method may comprise the steps of: receiving, from a network function (NF) related to data processing, reporting configuration information including collection configuration information related to data collection of the base station and information on reporting conditions for collected data of the base station; performing the data collection on the basis of the collection configuration information, wherein the collected data includes data related to a terminal connected to the base station; determining reporting of the collected data when the reporting conditions are satisfied; and transmitting a data reporting message including the collected data to the NF.

sources.title: METHODS AND SYSTEMS TO DEFINE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) BASED ADAPTIVE PROTOCOL FOR RADIO ACCESS NETWORK (RAN) [WO2026230966A1]
sources.abstract: The disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. Embodiments disclosed herein relate to methods (400) and systems for defining an Artificial Intelligence (AI) adaptive protocol for a Radio Access Network (RAN). The methods allow a User Equipment (UE) to request, and network to configure one or more radio parameters to be of dynamic nature, and use multiple values from pre-configured sets based on switching conditions. The methods allow the network to configure radio parameters along with a switching condition where the UE may switch parameter values with or without acknowledgement from the network. The methods provide a framework where radio configuration parameters can be of dynamically adapted based on contextual awareness. The methods provide correlation, and prediction exchange between the UE and network in order to arrive at inter-dependent parameter configuration, and dynamic set configurations.

sources.title: METHOD AND APPARATUS FOR ALLOCATING MAXIMUM POWER FOR COVERAGE EXPANSION [WO2026230903A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. A method for a base station, according to an embodiment of the present invention, may comprise the steps of: receiving, from a terminal, information about whether the terminal supports a low peak to average power ratio (PAPR) and information about whether the terminal supports a power boosting function for the low PAPR; determining whether to apply a low PAPR waveform to the terminal and whether to apply the power boosting function to the terminal, on the basis of whether the terminal supports the low PAPR and whether the terminal supports the power boosting function; if it is determined to apply the low PAPR waveform and the power boosting function to the terminal, transmitting configuration information for power boosting to the terminal; and receiving an uplink signal from the terminal.

sources.title: METHOD AND DEVICE FOR MONITORING PERFORMANCE OF CHANNEL STATE INFORMATION-REFERENCE SIGNAL COMPRESSION IN TERMINAL IN WIRELESS COMMUNICATION SYSTEM [WO2026230803A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting higher data transmission rates. A method performed by a terminal according to an embodiment of the present disclosure may comprise the steps of: receiving, from a base station, configuration information regarding CSI-RS compression; on the basis of the received configuration information, acquiring a compressed CSI-RS measurement value from a CSI-RS compressed through port combining or port sampling; reconstructing CSI for all CSI-RS ports by using an AI model on the basis of the compressed CSI-RS measurement value; measuring a performance monitoring metric by comparing the reconstructed CSI with CSI generated on the basis of a CSI-RS received from all CSI-RS ports of the base station; and reporting the measured performance monitoring metric to the base station.

sources.title: METHOD FOR SUPPORTING UPLINK SYNCHRONIZATION IN NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK AND APPARATUS SUPPORTING SAME [WO2026230964A1]
sources.abstract: Provided are a method for performing wireless communication and an apparatus supporting same. The method may comprise the steps of: receiving, by a first device, reference point information from a second device; acquiring, by the first device, first timing advance (TA) based on the reference point information; acquiring, by the first device, second TA for TA correction; and updating, by the first device, the second TA for TA correction, on the basis that the reference point information is updated.

sources.title: SUPPORTING MC SERVICE UE MANAGEMENT IN A WIRELESS COMMUNICATION SYSTEM [WO2026230806A1]
sources.abstract: The disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. The present disclosure provides methods and a system for supporting a MC service UE in a communication system. The method includes receiving a MC service authorization request from a MC service client (300). The MC service authorization request includes a MC service ID, a MC client ID, an IMPU, a public GRUU, a temporary GRUU, and a MC service UE label or a MC service UE identifier. Further, the method includes determining whether the MC service client (300) is authorized upon receiving the MC service authorization request. Further, the method includes storing a mapping between the MC service ID, the MC client ID, the IMPU, the public GRUU, the temporary GRUU, and the MC service UE label or the MC service UE identifier in a memory (104) of the MC service server (100) or in an external database (800), if the MC service client (300) is successfully authorized.

sources.title: SUPPORT OF USER PLANE MANAGEMENT ANALYTICS [WO2026230867A1]
sources.abstract: The disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. According to an aspect of the disclosure, there is provided a consumer NF in a wireless communication network and method thereof, the method comprising: transmitting, to a NWDAF, a message requesting or subscribing to user plane analytics from NWDAF; wherein the message includes request input information for requested analytics, and receiving, from the NWDAF, requested analytics including at least one of statistics or predictions on UP management analytics. According to another aspect of the disclosure, there is provided a NWDAF in a wireless communication network and method thereof, the method comprising: receiving, from a consumer NF, a message requesting or subscribing to user plane analytics, wherein the message includes request input information for requested analytics; determining the requested analytics based on the message, an operator policy, and an internal logic of the NWDAF; and transmitting, to the consumer NF, the requested analytics, the requested analytics including at least one of statistics or predictions on UP management analytics.

sources.title: MANAGING A SPATIAL MAP (SM) DATA SOURCE SUBSCRIPTION AT SM SERVER IN A COMMUNICATION NETWORK [WO2026230828A1]
sources.abstract: The disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting a higher data transmission rate. The present invention provides a method for managing a Spatial Map (SM) data source subscription at an SM server (101) in a communication network. The method enables the SM server (101) to receive a subscription request from a requester, including a VAL server or a SEAL server (301), and validate whether the requester is authorized based on security credentials. Upon successful authorization, the SM server (101) establishes a subscription associated with requester and stores corresponding subscription information. The method enables monitoring, based on subscribed event information, creation or deletion of an SM data source profile due to registration or de-registration of SM data sources, and changes in SM data source profile of SM data sources included in subscribed list. By transmitting subscription response including subscription identifier and indication of success or failure, the method improves secure subscription lifecycle management, event-driven monitoring, and efficient dissemination of relevant SM data source updates.

sources.title: METHOD AND DEVICE FOR PREDICTING FREQUENCY-AXIS CHANNEL IN WIRELESS COMMUNICATION SYSTEM [WO2026230823A1]
sources.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a 5G or 6G communication system for supporting higher data transmission rates. A method performed by a terminal in a wireless communication system comprises the steps of: receiving, from a base station, configuration information about a frequency resource of a channel state information reference signal, wherein the configuration information includes a bitmap indicating whether each of a plurality of subbands constituting the frequency resource corresponds to a to-be-measured subband or a to-be-predicted subband; receiving a CSI-RS from a base station in a first frequency band corresponding to the to-be-measured subband identified on the basis of the bitmap, and measuring a channel in the first frequency band on the basis of the received CSI-RS; predicting a channel in a second frequency band corresponding to the to-be-predicted subband by using an artificial intelligence model having, as an input, the measured channel of the first frequency band; generating channel state information on the basis of the measured channel of the first frequency band and the predicted channel of the second frequency band; and transmitting the generated CSI to the base station.

draft.summary: Research on 6G is growing quickly: OpenAlex works rose 43.9% from 2024 to 2025 and the year-to-date count is up 49.5% [S1, S2]. Patent filings are still rising but more slowly, and the year-to-date trend is flat at +7.9% [P1, P7]. Company filings show groundwork, requirements-setting and early R&D spending by Nokia, Qualcomm and Keysight, with no company reporting 6G products, customers or revenue [M1, M2, M4, M10]. Risk challenges weaken several science findings: the timeline is a forecast, most evidence is preprints and simulations, mid-band spectrum is already allocated, and no consensus on defining services exists [C1, C3, C9, R1, R2, S11]. The main uncertainty is whether standardization produces commercially compelling services and spectrum access by about 2030. Research volume alone does not show commercial success.
draft.plain_summary: 6G is the planned next generation of mobile networks, expected around 2030. Research and patent filings are growing, and some large companies are preparing, but nobody is selling 6G products yet. The biggest thing that could slow it down is that no one has identified a clear new service that justifies the cost, and that radio spectrum is already largely taken.

The evidence does not show which services will drive revenue, since consensus on killer services is lacking. Spectrum access depends on coexistence with incumbents. The evidence cannot support a view on long-term returns.

bull.label: forecast
bull.narrative: 3GPP standardization proceeds on schedule, and AI-native and NTN features create real upgrade demand. Operators and device makers raise R&D and test spending, and suppliers named in filings see 6G-related demand grow beyond the early R&D stage.

base.label: forecast
base.narrative: 6G stays in research and standardization through the near and medium term. It builds heavily on 5G Advanced, and revenue arrives gradually and late. Supplier exposure is a modest, hard-to-isolate part of broader 5G, AI and satellite demand.

bear.label: forecast
bear.narrative: Standards slip, spectrum coexistence limits capacity, and no killer service emerges. Much of the evidence is simulation and preprints that may not carry over to the field. Operators delay capital spending, and 6G-labelled R&D turns out to be mostly rebadged 5G work.
